Not only that, it is very frustrating when the receptionists ask what is wrong with you/what you need an appointment for and they take it upon themselves to decide 'how bad' you are and if you're worth an emergency appointment. Receptionists have no right to judge people like that as they are not Doctors. And when telling them personal information that should be confidential between patient and Doctor, they reply with a patronising "Uh you have that" type of response which is very unprofessional. Younger staff are quite pleasant but forget to do their job, so when you take a trip to the GP and your prescription isn't there it's time wasting and frustrating. You can see why the receptionists would be under stress with the new system in place, however, they should treat patients with more respect. If you ever get an appointment, the one to one experience with the Doctor is usually ok, but depending which Doctor it is, sometimes I leave feeling dissatisfied. I don't want to be one of those people to tell a Doctor how to do their job (because that would be stupid) but for example, surely it's common sense not to give someone who has an eating disorder and a BMI of 36, tablets that increase appetite and make you gain weight. The pharmacy staff next door however, are good workers and are run off their feet. They get prescriptions handed out almost instantly. It's very rare that I hear other people complaining to the pharmacy staff but when they do, it's due to the Doctor not sending the information over fast enough.

P.S. I agree with another comment also, it IS very embarrassing to get a call back from the Doctor and you have to talk about personal things in a public area. Furthermore, if you are only ill for a few days but need a Doctors note and can't get through to the receptionist, what the hell are you supposed to do? Eventually get an appointment and say "yeah I was ill last week and I need a Doctors note because I had time off work". It's
